persona.bio: Dani, 34, runs a mobile dog grooming van on her own in a suburb of Atlanta. Six or seven dogs a day. Clients book by text, and she answers the same questions all day: prices by breed, how long it takes, whether she does nails only, how to reschedule. She sends reminder texts the night before, writes a short note after each groom about matting or skin, and posts before and after photos on Instagram. Bookings live in a paper diary and her phone's calendar. She has never used AI.

steps.note: I run my own mobile dog grooming van. I handle bookings, appointment reminders, client messages and social posts from my phone, often between grooms. I write to dog owners who want a quick, friendly, clear answer. Keep a warm and plain tone, short sentences, and keep texts to two or three lines. Never add details I did not give you, like prices, openings or services I did not mention. Use square brackets for anything I need to fill in. Never promise a time slot for me. I read everything before I send it.

steps.title: Answering messages, saved once on your phone
steps.read: Your replies live on your phone’s keyboard. Each one is a few letters away, so you can answer from the van with wet hands and change only a name or a time. Your answers stay in your own voice, and you read each one before it goes out.

material.label: Your replies
items: Hi [first name], thanks for reaching out! Yes, [day and time] is open. Want me to book it for [dog’s name]?
Hi [first name], thanks for asking! [Day and time] is not open, but I have [other day and time]. Does that work?
Hi [first name], I’d be happy to help. The price depends on your dog’s size and coat. Can you tell me the breed and how long since the last groom?
Hi [first name], if [dog’s name] is matted, the groom can take longer and may cost more. I’ll check the coat when I arrive and talk with you first.
Hi [first name], no problem at all. I can move your appointment to [new day and time]. Does that work for you?
Hi [first name], thanks for letting me know. I’m with a dog right now and will reply properly as soon as I’m done. Talk soon!
Hi [first name], I’m on my way and will be there around [arrival time]. See you soon!

safeUse: Never type a client’s full name, home address, phone number or gate code into a chat tool. Use square brackets instead.
Keep your dog’s health details, like medical notes or medication, out of what you type. Write a general draft and add them yourself.
Do not type payment details or account numbers into a chat tool.
Read every reply, reminder and post before it goes out, and fix anything that is not right.
Check prices, openings and your own rules yourself, since the AI does not know them.

design.today: You answer client texts from the van, often right between grooms, with wet hands. Price and reschedule questions come in the same ones every day, many times a day.
design.newWay: Your most common replies are saved on your phone, so each one is a few letters away instead of typed from scratch. For a message that needs a little thought, like a matted poodle that may need a longer slot, you check your calendar and edit the saved reply before it goes. You read every reply and press send yourself, so the answers stay in your voice and are quicker to give between grooms.

steps.goal: Pick the ten questions clients ask you most, such as price, open slots, reschedules and matted coats.
Get ChatGPT ready on your phone so you can draft your replies there.
Turn your ten questions and your own past answers into short replies written in your voice, with gaps for the day, time and price.
Save the ten replies so each one is a few letters away when you answer a client.
Check the open slot in your calendar before you fill in the day and time in a reply.

design.checkPoint: You read every reply, fill in the day, time and price, and press send yourself.

design.today: You send reminder texts by hand, many times a day.
design.newWay: One saved reminder text sits on your phone, ready to use for each booking. You look at tomorrow's appointments in your calendar, bring up the reminder, fill in the client's name, dog and time, and send it. Every reminder stays consistent and takes far less typing, and nothing goes out unless you send it.
